item.aggregated_output:
# Analysis plan: sample-pca

Status: DRAFT

An analysis runs only after a person has read this file and approved it. Edit anything;
approval is what freezes it. After approval the plan is the record of intent -- change of
mind means a new analysis, not a quiet edit.

## Goal
Show how the six samples cluster using PCA on gene counts, coloured by condition. This is an exploratory view of sample relationships, with sample labels and the variance explained by each displayed component.

## Inputs
Artifact types resolve through each sub-stage's OUTPUTS.tsv at execution time; the paths
below are what they resolve to today.

| Artifact type | Resolved from | Path |
|---|---|---|
| counts_gene | rnaseq_bulk/01_nfcore-rnaseq-wrapper (native) | 02_bioinformatics/rnaseq_bulk/01_nfcore-rnaseq-wrapper/run/results/star_salmon/salmon.merged.gene_counts_length_scaled.tsv |
| design | 01_prepare_samplesheets (native) | 01_samplesheets/rnaseq_bulk_design.csv |

Paths are relative to the project. The design contains A1, A2, A3 (untreated) and B1, B2, B3 (treated).

## Method
1. After approval, write `scripts/sample_pca.py` and `scripts/submit.sh`. Run all analysis steps in the batch job using Python in `gars-bio`, with pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn and Matplotlib. Resolve `counts_gene` and `design` again with `_system/resolve_artifact.py --project <project> --assay rnaseq_bulk --consumes counts_gene design`; stop if resolution fails or the supplying artifacts differ from this plan.
2. Read the tab-separated native gene matrix and CSV design. Use `gene_id` as the feature identifier; exclude the annotation column `gene_name` from numeric data. Require unique gene identifiers and sample IDs, exactly the six design samples as matrix columns, non-missing conditions, finite nonnegative counts, and positive library totals. Match and reorder count columns by `sample_id`; stop on any mismatch. Preserve fractional counts without rounding.
3. Compute each sample's library total over all genes. Normalize to counts per million (CPM = count / library total * 1,000,000). Retain genes with CPM >= 1 in at least 3 of the 6 samples; transform retained values with log2(CPM + 1). Remove zero-variance genes, then select up to 2,000 genes with greatest sample variance (sample variance, ddof=1), breaking ties by gene_id. Stop if fewer than two variable genes remain. Record gene counts before and after each filter. This explicit library-size normalization and log transform prevents raw count magnitude from dominating PCA.
4. Transpose to samples by genes and run `sklearn.decomposition.PCA(n_components=5, svd_solver="full", whiten=False)`, which centres each gene without scaling it to unit variance. Use all six samples together; condition is only a plotting annotation and does not enter the PCA fit. No batch correction, sample exclusions or significance testing are planned.
5. Plot PC1 versus PC2 with Matplotlib: one point per sample, untreated blue (#0072B2), treated orange (#D55E00), individual sample ID labels, a condition legend and axis labels giving explained variance percentages. Export PNG at 300 dpi and a vector PDF. Save scores for all five PCs with sample IDs and conditions, plus explained variance and variance ratios for all five PCs.
6. Write a short report describing inputs, normalization, filtering, selected gene count, explained variance, tool versions and the descriptive scope of the plot. Record resolved input paths and SHA-256 hashes in the report. Do not infer biological mechanisms or statistical group separation from this exploratory figure. All generated files stay inside this analysis directory; input files remain read-only.

## Outputs
Types come from the closed vocabulary in _references/artifact_types.md.

| File | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| results/sample_pca.png | figure | Labelled PC1 versus PC2, coloured by condition, 300 dpi |
| results/sample_pca.pdf | figure | Vector version of the same PCA plot |
| results/pca_scores.csv | table | Six rows: sample_id, condition, PC1 through PC5 |
| results/pca_variance.csv | table | Component, explained variance, explained variance ratio and cumulative ratio |
| results/report.md | report | Method, filtering counts, provenance, tool versions and explained variance |

## Execution
Runs: batch
Submit `scripts/submit.sh` through `python3 <workspace>/_system/executorlib.py submit --workspace <project> <script>`, using the configured executor. Source `<workspace>/_system/gars-env.sh` and invoke `$GARS_PY` in the job. Target resources: 1 CPU, 4 GB RAM, 10 minutes; expected runtime under 5 minutes and result files under 10 MB. Use the existing environment without installing packages. Missing dependencies or invalid inputs cause a reported failure. After successful execution, run `stage03_analysis.py verify` to check all five declared files and register completion and provenance through the stage's normal history procedure.
# The workspace's batch executor (decision 0039). Seeded by stage 00; edit it per site.
#
# Required, not optional in spirit: GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never
# runs it in the current process (decision 0027). This file says WHICH scheduler. Delete it
# and the built-in Slurm descriptor below is what you get, byte for byte -- so an existing
# cluster workspace behaves exactly as it always has.
#
# The shape is deliberately narrow -- scalars, one-level lists, one-level `key: value` maps.
# `_system/` is stdlib-only (decision 0011), so this is parsed by a small parser we own, not
# by a YAML library. Do not reach for anchors, multi-line scalars or nested lists.
#
# Three doors, and nothing else:
#   header   the directives block the generated submit.sh opens with
#   submit   the argv that hands that GENERATED script to the scheduler -> a job id
#   status   the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED
#
# `submit_argv` runs the generated `submit.sh` and nothing else. It is not a place to add
# pipeline parameters, environment or wrapper logic: the audited parameter surface is
# `_config/<assay>.yaml`, and bypassing it is the one thing this file must never enable.

# The backend. `slurm` and `local` are built in; any other name means this file supplies the
# whole descriptor. (`local` runs the script detached on this machine and reports its PID --
# it is for testing the submit->status walk without a cluster, never a venue for analyses.)
name: slurm

# The directives block. Available placeholders, and only these:
#   {project} {assay} {substage} {partition} {time} {cpus} {mem}
# compute.partition / time / cpus / mem come from `_config/<assay>.yaml`.
directives:
  - "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}"
  - "#SBATCH --partition={partition}"
  - "#SBATCH --time={time}"
  - "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}"
  - "#SBATCH --mem={mem}"
  - "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out"
  - "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err"

# How a script becomes a job. {script} is the generated submit.sh; it must appear.
submit_argv:
  - sbatch
  - "{script}"

# How the job id is read back out of what submit printed. First capture group wins.
# A quoted value is taken verbatim -- there is no escape processing, so a regex is
# written exactly as a regex, single backslashes and all.
job_id_regex: "Submitted batch job (\d+)"

# How the job is asked after. {job_id} must appear.
status_argv:
  - sacct
  - -j
  - "{job_id}"
  - --format=State
  - --noheader

# This backend's states, mapped onto the closed vocabulary. Closed means closed: a state that
# is not listed here is refused by name rather than guessed at, so an unfamiliar scheduler
# state can never be silently read as success.
status_map:
  PENDING: PENDING
  CONFIGURING: PENDING
  REQUEUED: PENDING
  SUSPENDED: PENDING
  PREEMPTED: PENDING
  RUNNING: RUNNING
  COMPLETING: RUNNING
  RESIZING: RUNNING
  COMPLETED: COMPLETED
  FAILED: FAILED
  CANCELLED: FAILED
  TIMEOUT: FAILED
  NODE_FAIL: FAILED
  OUT_OF_MEMORY: FAILED
  BOOT_FAIL: FAILED
  DEADLINE: FAILED
  REVOKED: FAILED

# The Nextflow executor config this backend pairs with, under `_config/`. The wrapper checks
# it exists and carries no `params` block.
nextflow_config: nextflow.slurm.config

# The -profile the generated submit body passes to nextflow. A container runtime is a
# property of the venue, not of the science: this cluster runs apptainer. A venue that
# supplies each process's container itself (AWS Batch) sets it to "" (quoted -- a bare
# empty value reads as a section opener in the narrow parser), meaning no -profile.
nextflow_profile: apptainer
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The workspace's batch executor, as a setting rather than a spelling (decision 0039).

GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never runs it in the current process
(decision 0027). That ruling is scheduler-agnostic; only its spelling was Slurm-coupled --
`sbatch` lived in generated bytes and in contract prose, so a site without Slurm could not
run GARS at all.

This module is the one door. It reads `_config/executor.yaml` from the project and answers
three questions:

    header(...)          the directives block a generated submit.sh opens with
    submit(script)       the argv that hands that script to the scheduler -> a job id
    status(job_id)       the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED

No descriptor file, or `name: slurm`, means the built-in Slurm descriptor, whose bytes are
identical to what this system generated before the seam existed (pinned by a golden-bytes
test). A cluster that upgrades GARS notices nothing.

The built-in `local` backend runs the generated script under `nohup`-style detachment and
reports the PID as the job id. It exists so the deterministic core can exercise a real
submit -> status -> completion walk with no cluster at all; it is POSIX-only, like every
other assumption this system already makes, and it is NOT a venue for analyses -- stage 03's
venue gate is unchanged.

Runs on stock python 3.6.8, stdlib only, like every `_system/` helper.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

EXIT_OK, EXIT_FAILURE, EXIT_REFUSED, EXIT_USAGE = 0, 1, 2, 3

#: The closed state vocabulary every backend maps onto. A caller polls until it sees a
#: terminal state; nothing else is a legal answer.
STATES = ("PENDING", "RUNNING", "COMPLETED", "FAILED")

#: The placeholders a `directives` line may name. Anything else is a descriptor error, said
#: by name rather than raised as a KeyError from inside a format string.
HEADER_FIELDS = ("project", "assay", "substage", "partition", "time", "cpus", "mem")

DESCRIPTOR_NAME = "executor.yaml"

#: Where the `local` backend keeps what it needs to answer `status` for a PID it started.
LOCAL_JOBS_DIR = ".gars_local_jobs"

SLURM = {
    "name": "slurm",
    "directives": [
        "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}",
        "#SBATCH --partition={partition}",
        "#SBATCH --time={time}",
        "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}",
        "#SBATCH --mem={mem}",
        "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out",
        "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err",
    ],
    "submit_argv": ["sbatch", "{script}"],
    "job_id_regex": r"Submitted batch job (\d+)",
    "status_argv": ["sacct", "-j", "{job_id}", "--format=State", "--noheader"],
    "status_map": {
        "PENDING": "PENDING", "CONFIGURING": "PENDING", "REQUEUED": "PENDING",
        "SUSPENDED": "PENDING", "PREEMPTED": "PENDING",
        "RUNNING": "RUNNING", "COMPLETING": "RUNNING", "RESIZING": "RUNNING",
        "COMPLETED": "COMPLETED",
        "FAILED": "FAILED", "CANCELLED": "FAILED", "TIMEOUT": "FAILED",
        "NODE_FAIL": "FAILED", "OUT_OF_MEMORY": "FAILED", "BOOT_FAIL": "FAILED",
        "DEADLINE": "FAILED", "REVOKED": "FAILED",
    },
    "nextflow_config": "nextflow.slurm.config",
    #: The -profile the generated submit body passes to nextflow. A container runtime is a
    #: property of the venue, not of the science: this cluster runs apptainer; AWS Batch
    #: supplies each process's container itself and wants no profile at all (empty = omit).
    "nextflow_profile": "apptainer",
    "submit_note": "Slurm snapshots this script at submission: editing it never affects a "
                   "queued job.",
}

LOCAL = {
    "name": "local",
    "directives": [
        "# Executor: local. No scheduler directives -- this script is run directly, detached.",
        "# compute.* stays in the record: partition={partition} time={time} "
        "cpus={cpus} mem={mem}",
    ],
    "submit_argv": [],          # the local backend submits in-process, not through an argv
    "job_id_regex": "",
    "status_argv": [],
    "status_map": {},
    "nextflow_config": "",
    "nextflow_profile": "",
    "submit_note": "This script is run directly on this machine; editing it mid-run is a "
                   "race you will lose.",
}

BUILTINS = {"slurm": SLURM, "local": LOCAL}


# --- the descriptor ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _strip_value(raw):
    """A scalar: quoted span taken whole, otherwise up to an inline ` #` comment.

    Quoted first, deliberately: a Slurm directive line IS a comment (`#SBATCH ...`), so a
    naive comment strip would eat the descriptor's most important content.
    """
    raw = raw.strip()
    if raw[:1] in ('"', "'"):
        quote = raw[0]
        end = raw.find(quote, 1)
        if end != -1:
            return raw[1:end]
        return raw[1:]
    return re.split(r"\s+#", raw, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()


def parse_descriptor(text):
    """The narrow parser for a template we own -- scalars, one-level lists, one-level maps.

    The same trade `wrapperlib.read_config` makes (decision 0011): stdlib-only means no YAML
    library, and the template's shape is fixed and documented in the template itself.
    """
    values = {}
    section = None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):\s*(.*)$", raw)
        if m:
            key, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            if rest.strip():
                values[key] = _strip_value(rest)
                section = None
            else:
                section = key
                values[key] = None      # shape decided by the first child line
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^\s+-\s+(.*)$", raw)
        if m and section:
            if not isinstance(values.get(section), list):
                values[section] = []
            values[section].append(_strip_value(m.group(1)))
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):\s*(.*)$", raw)
        if m and section:
            if not isinstance(values.get(section), dict):
                values[section] = {}
            values[section][m.group(1)] = _strip_value(m.group(2))
            continue
    return values


def descriptor_path(config_root):
    return Path(config_root) / "_config" / DESCRIPTOR_NAME


def load(config_root):
    """The descriptor for a project. Absent file -> the built-in Slurm descriptor.

    `config_root` is the directory that owns `_config/` -- the project, in GARS's layout.
    """
    path = descriptor_path(config_root)
    if not path.is_file():
        return dict(SLURM)
    parsed = parse_descriptor(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    name = parsed.get("name") or "slurm"
    base = dict(BUILTINS.get(name, {"name": name}))
    for key, value in parsed.items():
        if value is not None:
            base[key] = value
    base.setdefault("name", name)
    return base


def validate(descriptor):
    """Problems with a descriptor, in member words. Empty list means usable."""
    problems = []
    name = descriptor.get("name")
    if not name:
        problems.append("the descriptor has no `name:` line; name the backend "
                        "(slurm, local, or your own)")
    directives = descriptor.get("directives")
    if directives is not None and not isinstance(directives, list):
        problems.append("`directives:` must be a list of `- \"...\"` lines")
    elif isinstance(directives, list):
        for line in directives:
            for field in re.findall(r"\{([A-Za-z_]+)\}", line):
                if field not in HEADER_FIELDS:
                    problems.append("directive line names {%s}, which this system does not "
                                    "supply; available: %s"
                                    % (field, ", ".join("{%s}" % f for f in HEADER_FIELDS)))
    if name not in BUILTINS:
        submit_argv = descriptor.get("submit_argv")
        if not isinstance(submit_argv, list) or not submit_argv:
            problems.append("`submit_argv:` must be a non-empty list; it runs the GENERATED "
                            "script and nothing else")
        elif not any("{script}" in a for a in submit_argv):
            problems.append("`submit_argv:` never names {script}; the generated submit.sh is "
                            "the only thing a descriptor may submit")
        status_argv = descriptor.get("status_argv")
        if not isinstance(status_argv, list) or not status_argv:
            problems.append("`status_argv:` must be a non-empty list naming {job_id}")
        elif not any("{job_id}" in a for a in status_argv):
            problems.append("`status_argv:` never names {job_id}")
        if not descriptor.get("job_id_regex"):
            problems.append("`job_id_regex:` is required: it is how the submit output "
                            "becomes a job id")
        else:
            try:
                re.compile(descriptor["job_id_regex"])
            except re.error as exc:
                problems.append("`job_id_regex:` does not compile (%s) -- remember the "
                                "parser takes a quoted value verbatim, with no escape "
                                "processing; a regex needing a double quote must be "
                                "single-quoted" % exc)
        status_map = descriptor.get("status_map")
        if not isinstance(status_map, dict) or not status_map:
            problems.append("`status_map:` must map this backend's states onto %s"
                            % "|".join(STATES))
        else:
            unknown = sorted({v for v in status_map.values() if v not in STATES})
            if unknown:
                problems.append("`status_map:` maps onto %s, which are not in the closed "
                                "vocabulary %s" % (", ".join(unknown), "|".join(STATES)))
    return problems


# --- the three doors ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _fill(text, fields):
    """Substitute the KNOWN {tokens} and leave every other brace alone.

    Deliberately not str.format: a descriptor element may legitimately contain literal
    braces -- the awsbatch submit argv carries a JSON --container-overrides payload, and
    format() reads {"command": ...} as a placeholder named \'"command"\' and crashes. The
    descriptor is data, not a template language; only the documented tokens are tokens.
    """
    for key, value in fields.items():
        text = text.replace("{%s}" % key, str(value))
    return text


def header_lines(config_root, cfg, project, assay, substage, descriptor=None):
    """The directives block, rendered. Returns a list of lines with no trailing newlines."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    fields = {
        "project": project,
        "assay": assay,
        "substage": str(Path(substage).resolve()),
        "partition": cfg.get("compute.partition", "{partition}"),
        "time": cfg.get("compute.time", "{time}"),
        "cpus": cfg.get("compute.cpus", "{cpus}"),
        "mem": cfg.get("compute.mem", "{mem}"),
    }
    return [_fill(line, fields) for line in descriptor.get("directives") or []]


DEFAULT_SUBMIT_NOTE = ("The scheduler snapshots this script at submission: editing it never "
                       "affects a queued job.")


def submit_note(descriptor):
    """The one line the generated submit.sh says about editing itself, per backend."""
    return descriptor.get("submit_note") or DEFAULT_SUBMIT_NOTE


def config_root_for(path):
    """The nearest ancestor that owns `_config/` -- a sub-stage or analysis dir's project.

    Walked rather than counted: stage 02 sub-stages sit three levels down and stage 03
    analyses two, and a seam that hard-codes either depth breaks the other.
    """
    here = Path(path).resolve()
    for candidate in [here] + list(here.parents):
        if (candidate / "_config").is_dir():
            return candidate
    return here


def submit_argv(descriptor, script):
    return [_fill(a, {"script": script}) for a in descriptor.get("submit_argv") or []]


def status_argv(descriptor, job_id):
    return [_fill(a, {"job_id": job_id}) for a in descriptor.get("status_argv") or []]


def nextflow_config_path(config_root, descriptor=None):
    """The nextflow config file this workspace's executor pairs with, or None.

    The descriptor names it (0039); callers must never spell `nextflow.slurm.config`
    themselves -- that name is the Slurm default, not a law.
    """
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    name = descriptor.get("nextflow_config") or ""
    return (Path(config_root) / "_config" / name) if name else None


def nextflow_profile(config_root, descriptor=None):
    """The -profile the generated submit body passes, '' meaning none."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    value = descriptor.get("nextflow_profile")
    return SLURM["nextflow_profile"] if value is None else value


def submit_command(config_root, script, descriptor=None):
    """The literal command line `reproducibility/commands.sh` records for this workspace."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    if descriptor.get("name") == "local":
        return "python3 %s/_system/executorlib.py submit --workspace %s %s" % (
            "$WS", str(config_root), str(script))
    argv = submit_argv(descriptor, script)
    return " ".join(argv) if argv else str(script)


def _local_jobs_dir(config_root):
    return Path(config_root) / LOCAL_JOBS_DIR


#: The one-liner the `local` backend detaches. The outer shell backgrounds a subshell and
#: prints its PID, then exits -- so nothing is left for this process to wait on (no orphaned
#: Popen handle, no ResourceWarning) and the job outlives the caller, which is the point.
#: The GROUP's own descriptors go to /dev/null, not just each command's: a backgrounded job
#: inherits the caller's stdout pipe, and a pipe that stays open is a submit that blocks
#: until the job finishes -- which is exactly the thing a scheduler must never do.
LOCAL_RUNNER = ('{ bash "$1" >> "$2" 2>&1; echo $? > "$3"; } '
                '</dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &\necho $!\n')


def _local_submit(config_root, script):
    """Start the generated script detached; the PID is the job id.

    POSIX-only by construction, which is the posture GARS already has. The exit code lands in
    a sidecar beside the script so `status` can tell COMPLETED from FAILED once the process
    is gone -- a PID alone cannot say how a job ended.
    """
    script = Path(script).resolve()
    jobs = _local_jobs_dir(config_root)
    jobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    log = script.parent / (script.name + ".local.log")
    exit_file = script.parent / (script.name + ".local.exit")
    if exit_file.is_file():
        exit_file.unlink()          # a re-submit must never read the previous run's verdict
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", "-c", LOCAL_RUNNER, "gars-local", str(script), str(log), str(exit_file)],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    job_id = (proc.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
    if not job_id.isdigit():
        return None
    with open(str(jobs / ("%s.json" % job_id)), "w") as fh:
        json.dump({"script": str(script), "log": str(log), "exit_file": str(exit_file)},
                  fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    return job_id


def _local_status(config_root, job_id):
    record = _local_jobs_dir(config_root) / ("%s.json" % job_id)
    if not record.is_file():
        return "FAILED"             # nothing here started that job; say so, never guess
    exit_file = Path(json.loads(record.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["exit_file"])
    if exit_file.is_file():
        return "COMPLETED" if exit_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() == "0" else "FAILED"
    try:
        os.kill(int(job_id), 0)
        return "RUNNING"
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    return "FAILED"


def submit(config_root, script, descriptor=None):
    """Hand the generated script to the scheduler. Returns (job_id, detail-or-None)."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    if descriptor.get("name") == "local":
        job_id = _local_submit(config_root, script)
        return (job_id, None) if job_id else (None, "the local backend printed no PID")
    argv = submit_argv(descriptor, script)
    if not argv:
        return None, "the descriptor names no submit_argv"
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    except OSError as exc:
        return None, "cannot run %s: %s" % (argv[0], exc)
    out = (proc.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    err = (proc.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None, "%s exited %d: %s" % (argv[0], proc.returncode, (err or out).strip())
    try:
        m = re.search(descriptor.get("job_id_regex") or r"(\d+)", out)
    except re.error as exc:
        return None, "job_id_regex does not compile: %s" % exc
    if not m:
        return None, "no job id in the submit output: %r" % out.strip()
    return m.group(1), None


def status(config_root, job_id, descriptor=None):
    """Ask after a job. Returns (state, detail-or-None); state is one of STATES."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    if descriptor.get("name") == "local":
        return _local_status(config_root, job_id), None
    argv = status_argv(descriptor, job_id)
    if not argv:
        return None, "the descriptor names no status_argv"
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    except OSError as exc:
        return None, "cannot run %s: %s" % (argv[0], exc)
    out = (proc.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None, "%s exited %d" % (argv[0], proc.returncode)
    raw = ""
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            raw = line.strip()
            break
    # `CANCELLED by 1234` and `COMPLETED+` are the shapes sacct actually prints.
    token = raw.split()[0].rstrip("+").upper() if raw else ""
    mapped = (descriptor.get("status_map") or {}).get(token)
    if not mapped:
        return None, "unmapped backend state %r -- add it to status_map" % (token or raw)
    return mapped, None


# --- CLI ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def emit(result, code):
    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    return code


def main(argv=None):
    # `--workspace` is accepted on either side of the subcommand: the contracts write it
    # after (`... submit --workspace <project> <script>`), a shell habit writes it before.
    common = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    common.add_argument("--workspace", default=argparse.SUPPRESS,
                        help="the project directory that owns _config/")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="The workspace's batch executor (0039).",
                                     parents=[common])
    parser.set_defaults(workspace=".")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")

    p_header = sub.add_parser("header", parents=[common],
                              help="print the generated submit.sh directives block")
    p_header.add_argument("--project", default="{project}")
    p_header.add_argument("--assay", default="{assay}")
    p_header.add_argument("--substage", default=".")
    for key in ("partition", "time", "cpus", "mem"):
        p_header.add_argument("--" + key, default=None)

    p_submit = sub.add_parser("submit", parents=[common],
                              help="submit a GENERATED submit.sh")
    p_submit.add_argument("script")

    p_status = sub.add_parser("status", parents=[common],
                              help="the state of a submitted job")
    p_status.add_argument("job_id")

    sub.add_parser("describe", parents=[common],
                   help="the resolved descriptor and any problems with it")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not args.command:
        parser.print_help()
        return EXIT_USAGE

    root = Path(args.workspace)
    descriptor = load(root)
    problems = validate(descriptor)
    result = {"command": args.command, "executor": descriptor.get("name"),
              "descriptor": str(descriptor_path(root)),
              "descriptor_present": descriptor_path(root).is_file()}

    if args.command == "describe":
        result["resolved"] = descriptor
        result["problems"] = problems
        result["ok"] = not problems
        return emit(result, EXIT_OK if not problems else EXIT_REFUSED)

    if problems:
        result["problems"] = problems
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    if args.command == "header":
        cfg = {}
        for key in ("partition", "time", "cpus", "mem"):
            value = getattr(args, key)
            if value:
                cfg["compute." + key] = value
        result["header"] = header_lines(root, cfg, args.project, args.assay, args.substage,
                                        descriptor=descriptor)
        return emit(result, EXIT_OK)

    if args.command == "submit":
        job_id, detail = submit(root, args.script, descriptor=descriptor)
        if job_id is None:
            result["error"] = detail
            return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)
        result["job_id"] = job_id
        result["ok"] = True
        return emit(result, EXIT_OK)

    if args.command == "status":
        state, detail = status(root, args.job_id, descriptor=descriptor)
        if state is None:
            result["error"] = detail
            return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)
        result["job_id"] = args.job_id
        result["state"] = state
        result["terminal"] = state in ("COMPLETED", "FAILED")
        return emit(result, EXIT_OK)

    return EXIT_USAGE


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Configuration for assay rnaseq_bulk, project run-4c866bac
#
# Stage 00 put this here so you never author a config from a blank file. Everything that can be
# filled in for you already has been. What remains is marked <REQUIRED> -- those are scientific
# decisions, and no stage will substitute a value for them, because a wrong one produces a
# confident wrong answer rather than an error.
#
# Full rationale for every key: _references/config_schema.md

# --- what the reads are ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# auto | forward | reverse | unstranded
# `auto` delegates to nf-core's RSeQC check, which cannot return a confident *stranded* call on an
# unstranded library and reports it as "N/N samples failed strandedness check" -- a warning that
# reads like a failure and is not one. Set it explicitly if the library prep is known.
# This lab's measured answer (decision 0032): the TALL leukemia libraries are UNSTRANDED --
# RSeQC sense ~= antisense on 10/10 samples, corroborated by the lab's sns run. For those
# libraries set `unstranded` explicitly and the warning disappears.
strandedness: auto

# --- what to align against ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Declare EITHER `genome` OR `fasta` + `gtf`, never both.
#
# Do NOT use `genome: GRCh38`. That resolves to the NCBI iGenomes build, which carries no
# `gene_biotype` attribute, and the run fails at SUBREAD_FEATURECOUNTS *after* counts are written.
# It cost a full pipeline run once (decision 0005, failure 5). Use the Ensembl FASTA + GTF.
reference:
  # You do not need to fill these by hand: stage 02 offers the registered genomes as a menu and
  # sets fasta, gtf and derived_dir together, so they can never be mismatched. Paste paths here
  # only if you are using a reference that is not in _references/genomes.md.
  fasta: <REQUIRED: choose a genome at stage 02, or paste a FASTA path>
  gtf:   <REQUIRED: choose a genome at stage 02, or paste the matching GTF path>

  # Optional but strongly recommended: a cache of built STAR/Salmon indices, keyed by PIPELINE
  # version. Without it every run rebuilds ~43 GB of indices, about 40 minutes. A STAR index is
  # rejected by a different STAR version, which is why the version is part of the path.
  # derived_dir: ~/install/refs/ensembl-GRCh38-116/derived/nf-core-rnaseq-3.26.0

aligner: star_salmon          # star_salmon | star_rsem | hisat2 | bowtie2_salmon

# --- where it runs -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Infrastructure, not science. These are the values verified on this cluster; change them if your
# allocation differs.
compute:
  partition: cpu_long
  time: "5-00:00:00"
  cpus: 8
  mem: 64G
  # Nextflow's scratch. NEVER inside the project: a single 10-sample run accumulates 250-350 GB
  # here, because work/ retains every process output so -resume can reuse it. results/ is
  # published with mode 'copy', so work/ is disposable once a run succeeds.
  work_dir: /gpfs/scratch/javier/gars-work/run-4c866bac

# --- what question the differential expression asks --------------------------------------------
# Read by sub-stage 02.02. Every formula term must be a column of the design table
# (01_samplesheets/rnaseq_bulk_design.csv), and both contrast levels must appear in that column.
de:
  # Also offered as choices at stage 02: the contrast menu lists the levels your design table
  # actually contains, in both directions, and refuses one whose level has fewer than 2 samples.
  formula:  <REQUIRED: defaults to "~ condition"; use "~ batch + condition" to control for batch>
  contrast: <REQUIRED: choose at stage 02, or write factor,numerator,denominator e.g. "condition,MT,WT">

analysis = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
project = analysis.parent.parent
workspace = project.parent.parent
expected = {
    'counts_gene': '02_bioinformatics/rnaseq_bulk/01_nfcore-rnaseq-wrapper/run/results/star_salmon/salmon.merged.gene_counts_length_scaled.tsv',
    'design': '01_samplesheets/rnaseq_bulk_design.csv',
}
resolved = json.loads(subprocess.check_output([
    sys.executable, str(workspace / '_system/resolve_artifact.py'),
    '--project', str(project), '--assay', 'rnaseq_bulk',
    '--consumes', 'counts_gene', 'design']))
assert resolved['ok'], resolved
for kind, path in expected.items():
    assert resolved['resolved'][kind]['resolved'] == path, 'Input resolution changed'
    assert resolved['resolved'][kind]['role'] == 'native'
raw = {kind: (project / path).read_bytes() for kind, path in expected.items()}
header = next(csv.reader(io.StringIO(raw['counts_gene'].decode()), delimiter='\\t'))
assert len(header) == len(set(header)), 'Duplicate matrix columns'
counts = pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(raw['counts_gene']), sep='\\t', dtype={'gene_id': str})
design = pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(raw['design']), dtype=str)
assert not counts['gene_id'].isna().any() and counts['gene_id'].is_unique
assert design['sample_id'].is_unique and not design['sample_id'].isna().any()
assert not design['condition'].isna().any() and design['condition'].str.strip().ne('').all()
ids = design['sample_id'].tolist()
expected_conditions = {'A1': 'untreated', 'A2': 'untreated', 'A3': 'untreated', 'B1': 'treated', 'B2': 'treated', 'B3': 'treated'}
assert dict(zip(ids, design['condition'])) == expected_conditions

matrix = counts.set_index('gene_id')[ids].astype(float)
assert np.isfinite(matrix.to_numpy()).all() and (matrix >= 0).all().all()
totals = matrix.sum(axis=0)
assert (totals > 0).all()
cpm = matrix.div(totals, axis=1) * 1e6
keep = (cpm >= 1).sum(axis=1) >= 3
logged = np.log2(cpm.loc[keep] + 1)
variance = logged.var(axis=1, ddof=1)
variable = variance[variance > 0]
assert len(variable) >= 2, 'Fewer than two variable genes'
rank = pd.DataFrame({'gene_id': variable.index, 'variance': variable.values}).sort_values(['variance', 'gene_id'], ascending=[False, True])
selected = rank.head(2000)['gene_id'].tolist()
pca = PCA(n_components=5, svd_solver='full', whiten=False)
scores = pca.fit_transform(logged.loc[selected].T.to_numpy())

score_table = design[['sample_id', 'condition']].copy()
for i in range(5):
    score_table['PC%d' % (i + 1)] = scores[:, i]
score_table.to_csv(results / 'pca_scores.csv', index=False)
pd.DataFrame({'component': ['PC%d' % (i + 1) for i in range(5)], 'explained_variance': pca.explained_variance_, 'explained_variance_ratio': pca.explained_variance_ratio_, 'cumulative_ratio': np.cumsum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)}).to_csv(results / 'pca_variance.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
for condition, colour in [('untreated', '#0072B2'), ('treated', '#D55E00')]:
    mask = design['condition'].eq(condition).to_numpy()
    ax.scatter(scores[mask, 0], scores[mask, 1], c=colour, label=condition, s=65)
for i, sample in enumerate(ids):
    ax.annotate(sample, (scores[i, 0], scores[i, 1]), xytext=(5, 5), textcoords='offset points')
ax.set_xlabel('PC1 (%.2f%%)' % (100 * pca.explained_variance_ratio_[0]))
ax.set_ylabel('PC2 (%.2f%%)' % (100 * pca.explained_variance_ratio_[1]))
ax.set_title('Sample PCA on gene counts')
ax.legend(title='Condition')
ax.margins(0.18)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(results / 'sample_pca.png', dpi=300)
fig.savefig(results / 'sample_pca.pdf')
plt.close(fig)
report = ['# Sample PCA', '', 'Six samples; condition is used only for plot annotation.', '', 'Library totals were calculated over all genes; counts were normalized to CPM. Genes with CPM >= 1 in at least three samples were transformed with log2(CPM + 1). Zero-variance genes were removed; up to 2,000 genes were selected by descending sample variance (ddof=1), with ties broken by gene_id. PCA centres genes without unit-variance scaling (full SVD, five components, no whitening).', '', 'Genes: input %d; after CPM filter %d; after zero-variance filter %d; selected %d.' % (len(matrix), int(keep.sum()), len(variable), len(selected)), '', '## Explained variance', '']
for i, ratio in enumerate(pca.explained_variance_ratio_):
    report.append('- PC%d: %.4f%%' % (i + 1, ratio * 100))
report += ['', '## Input provenance', '']
for kind, path in expected.items():
    report += ['- %s: "'`%s`; SHA-256 `%s`.'"' % (kind, path, hashlib.sha256(raw[kind]).hexdigest())]
report += ['', '## Software', '', 'Python %s; pandas %s; NumPy %s; scikit-learn %s; Matplotlib %s.' % (sys.version.split()[0], pd.__version__, np.__version__, sklearn.__version__, matplotlib.__version__), '', 'This exploratory figure describes sample relationships. It provides no significance test of group separation or inference about biological mechanisms. No samples were excluded and no batch correction was applied.', '']
(results / 'report.md').write_text('\\n'.join(report))
